transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-07-21
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (NovaPay Head of ML), Aisha (Platform), Tom (Product), Leah (SRE)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — same agenda as last week: review throughput numbers, tuning changes we put in, and next steps for the canary. Priya and I will walk through results.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll jump in with the experiments we ran overnight. We focused on continuous batching parameters and raising the concurrency target. Baseline from last week was concurrency=8, batch target 512 tokens, p95 latency ~210ms, and sustained tokens/sec ~42k on the dedicated 8xA100-ish nodes you provided.
[00:55] Carlos (NovaPay): Quick clarify — that 42k tokens/sec is measured at the model server layer or end-to-end including our network hop? We want end-to-end numbers for SLI alignment.
[01:10] Priya (Redwood SE): Good call — the 42k is server-side decode throughput. End-to-end for your trace was about 36k tokens/sec because of the 35-40ms extra network RTT and the prefix decoding in your gateway. We'll share the breakdown sheet.
[01:30] Tom (Product): And latency percentiles? p50/p95/p99? Those are the product constraints.
[01:42] Priya: p50 ~90ms, p95 ~210ms, p99 ~480ms in the baseline. When we bumped concurrency to 12 and adjusted continuous batch window from 8ms to 16ms we saw throughput increase to ~96k tokens/sec server-side but p95 rose slightly to ~260ms during peak. p99 still spiky for very long sequences.
[02:15] Aisha (Platform): Wait, doubling throughput? That seems, like, big. Did you change quantization or anything else?
[02:25] Priya: No model quantization changes; same 4-bit profile. The main wins were better batching packing (we tuned the packer to be more aggressive for similar sequence lengths) and increasing the concurrent request slots which allows the runtime to fill batches more consistently. Also we enabled the KV-cache sticky routing for warm sessions which improved reuse.
[02:50] Carlos: What about cold-starts? Our users have a mix of short chats and some long-lived sessions. Cold starts kill p95.
[03:00] Priya: Cold-starts are still the pain point. We observed warm sessions hitting KV-cache hit rates ~78% after 2-3 requests, but initial requests obviously see full decode cost. For that, we suggested a tiny warmup reserve — keep 3 warm worker slots per zone for your high-QPS routes. That adds cost but reduces p95 on first request by ~60ms.
[03:25] Leah (SRE): On warm worker slots, do we need special orchestration? How's that handled in Redwood Dedicated? Is it auto or manual?
[03:35] Jordan: You can configure warm pools in Redwood Dedicated. It's part of the autoscale policy — you set min_active_workers and warm_reserve. Priya, maybe show the autoscale tweak we used.
[03:45] Priya: Right — we set min_active_workers to 6 and warm_reserve to 3. That kept tail latencies down during our 1-hour spike test. Cost-wise it's a small increase; Jordan will send the delta.
[04:10] Tom: Can you show the queueing behaviour? When you increased concurrency, did queue length grow a lot and cause head-of-line blocking?
[04:20] Priya: Good question. We instrumented the request queue — with concurrency=12 we did see longer queue waiting times for very bursty arrivals, but because batches were larger the throughput per GPU improved and the average wait for queued requests dropped after the initial warm window. There's a tradeoff: more concurrency increases batching efficiency but can increase per-request wait if bursts exceed the window. We recommend a max_queue_ms of 120ms for your traffic pattern.
[04:55] Carlos: Any mis-transcription — sorry — I mean, any observed request timeouts or dropped calls at that setting? We have strict SLAs.
[05:05] Priya: No hard timeouts in our runs, but we saw a handful of 504-style upstream gateway timeouts tied to your gateway config at high burst rates. We recommend your gateway increase upstream timeout to 10s during canary. Also consider a local retry policy with jitter to avoid thundering herds.
[05:35] Aisha: Regarding KV-cache — you mentioned sticky routing. How does that interact with autoscaling and node failures? If a worker dies won't we lose affinity and see cold cache penalties?
[05:50] Priya: Correct. We use a soft affinity: requests prefer the same worker for session groups but will fallback when that worker is out of capacity. When autoscaling removes nodes we gracefully drain sessions and attempt KV snapshot transfer where possible; there's a short window of cold penalty. The mitigation is to use the warm_reserve and shorter snapshot intervals.
[06:15] Carlos: Do you have numbers for cost vs latency tradeoff if we go with a bigger warm reserve and higher concurrency? We need to present to our CFO.
[06:26] Jordan: We'll provide a spreadsheet showing cost per 1M tokens for three configs: conservative (concurrency=8, minimal warm_reserve), performance (concurrency=12, warm_reserve=3), and aggressive (concurrency=16, warm_reserve=6). Expect the performance profile to be ~1.9-2.3x cheaper per token vs conservative due to batching wins but with slightly higher average latency during spikes. We'll send that today.
[06:55] Priya: Also note that caching + batching together compound — the more cache hits, the fewer tokens decoded so throughput numbers improve non-linearly. In one run we saw effective token reduction by ~18% because of prefix reuse.
[07:12] Tom: Any red flags for compliance or security when using warm reserves / sticky routing?
[07:20] Jordan: No new controls needed; Dedicated still enforces network isolation, KMS integration for key material, and audit logs. We'll share the SOC2 docs if your compliance folks want them.
[07:35] Carlos: Ok good. For the next run can we try concurrency=12 but with max_queue_ms=100 and the warm_reserve set to 3? Also capture KV-hit over time and per-session latencies.
[07:48] Priya: Yep. We'll run an extended 6-hour throughput test with your real traces if you share them. That will exercise diurnal patterns and long tail behaviors.
[08:00] Aisha: We'll upload the trace by EOD tomorrow. Any instrumentation we should add?
[08:07] Priya: If you can include original request timestamps and session id hash it helps. Also include sequence length per request and any user priority flags. We'll annotate results per route.
[08:25] Leah: For the canary, what's the rollback plan if p99 spikes above our SLA?
[08:33] Jordan: Canary config will be small — 5% of traffic. We'll set automatic fallback to the slower conservative model variant and lower concurrency if p99 breaches threshold for 5 minutes. That rollback is automated by route policy. Priya will prepare the rollout JSON for your infra team.
[08:55] Carlos: Great. Quick question about model variants — are you recommending we use a slightly smaller model for lower-cost fallbacks?
[09:03] Priya: Exactly. We recommend a compatible variant with fewer layers quantized more aggressively for fallback; Redwood's routing will swap to that variant when capacity constrained. We saw a smooth degradation in our tests.
[09:20] Tom: Anything else on batching heuristics? We saw some users with very long sequences that reduce packing efficiency.
[09:28] Priya: For heterogeneous seq lengths we enable length-bucket packing so similar-length requests are batched. That avoids padding waste. For very long tails we recommend a separate long-sequence route with lower concurrency to avoid head-of-line effects.
[09:50] Jordan: Alright — recap and next steps: Priya runs the 6-hour test with concurrency=12, max_queue_ms=100, warm_reserve=3. Jordan sends pricing and the benchmark spreadsheet. NovaPay shares request traces. We'll aim to schedule canary after validating results.
[10:10] Carlos: Sounds good. Also please share the test artifacts link and the benchmark spreadsheet; we'll review and book an internal review with finance.
[10:22] Priya: I'll upload the run logs, flame graphs, and KV-hit timeline to the shared folder. Link (shared): https://redwood.example.com/shared/novapay/poc/throughput-2027-07-21 (note: link is placeholder)
[10:35] Jordan: Thanks folks, we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invite for Friday if the test looks green.
[10:45] End of meeting.

Notes: Transcription includes some auto-fill errors (Speaker 5 present as low-confidence). Some technical terms transcribed inconsistently ("K V cache" vs "KV cache").
